title: Object
summary: An object is whatever a chosen mathematical discourse permits us to refer to as one thing.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared preformal metalanguage context is fixed.

content.plain: An object is whatever a chosen mathematical discourse permits us to refer to as one thing.
content.exact: Object is a role in a framework, not a universal substance. A framework supplies a domain U of admissible referents and rules for forming or recognizing them.
content.example: A number, function, proof, graph, or group may each be an object in a suitable framework.
content.caveat: Different foundations encode the same informal object differently.
